reading_limits: Read the displayed theorem scopes, constructions, examples and residual comparisons in these chapters and the fixed synthesis already used by their authors. This is editorial synthesis, not a new independent proof of their mathematical sources.
elementary_calculation: Chapter17 gives complete matrix-unit inverses in17.3 and an elementary module-category distinction.

narrow_review_repairs.before: Every finite number of radial inputs is already covered by the theorem in Chapter 8, on the declared \(F((q))\) domain and original jointly nilpotent smooth tests.
narrow_review_repairs.after: Under the coherent realization, full-unit, bounded-below cellularity and two-term inflated-descent hypotheses stated in Chapter 8, its theorem covers every finite number of radial inputs on the declared \(F((q))\) domain and original jointly nilpotent smooth tests.

narrow_review_repairs.before: The available analytic theorem constructs normalized boundary maps, finite uncut tree compositions and identity insertions on specified completions.
narrow_review_repairs.after: Under the normalized boundary hypothesis of Chapter 10—convergent algebraic four-point channel sewings, canonical spectral \(L^2\) channel vectors, the prescribed real unitary fusion transformation and normalized positive-label pentagon—and its two-radius estimates, the available analytic theorem constructs finite uncut tree compositions and identity insertions on specified completions.

narrow_review_repairs.before: **Problem 18.10.** Establish positivity of the complete Weil functional on every compact smooth test, or construct an independently defined ordinary positive representation whose trace is that complete functional.
narrow_review_repairs.after:
**Problem 18.10.** Establish
\[
W(g*g^*)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C),
\]
or construct an independently defined ordinary positive representation whose trace is the complete Weil functional on its stated test algebra.
